title: Normalize dedicated capacity usage signals and SLA offset accounting
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: Multiple sources (runtime token counters, edge rate-limiters, autoscaler logs) produce conflicting per-tenant usage numbers for Dedicated GPU pools. This causes three observable issues: 1) burst consumption is either undercounted (customers billed less than actual reserved usage) or double-counted when requests traverse multiple proxies, 2) SLA credit computation windows diverge from billing windows leading to incorrect credit amounts, and 3) reconciliation jobs produce frequent manual adjustments between committed throughput and billed tokens. Goal: implement a canonical usage normalization pipeline and deterministic SLA offset calculation so billed usage, real-time quotas, and SLA credits align within an acceptable tolerance, remove need for manual monthly corrections, and provide transparent dashboards for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical event stream created: all serving runtime, edge gateway, and autoscaler usage events correlate to a single deduped usage record per request (trace_id or dedupe_id)
End-to-end billed token delta vs runtime-produced tokens <= 0.5% for sampled tenants across a 7-day window
Burst accounting: bursts consumed from burst budget are visible in billing UI and reconcile to burst_pool metrics (no negative or double-counted burst tokens)
SLA credits computed using aligned hourly buckets that match billing windows; credit amounts match manual audit for 3 historical incidents
Automated reconciliation job removes need for manual adjustments; monthly reconciliation runs with zero manual entries for pilot tenants
Canary rollout executed to 10 pilot tenants with approval from Finance and Customer Success before full release
implementation_notes: Introduce 'usage_event_v2' protobuf with fields: tenant_id, pool_id, timestamp_ms, token_count, dedupe_id, path_hint, decision_flags (reserved|burst|fallback)
Instrument runtime and gateway to emit dedupe_id: prefer tracing.trace_id when available, fallback to hashed request fingerprint
Add ingestion lambda that performs idempotent upserts into canonical usage table keyed by (tenant_id, dedupe_id, hour_bucket)
Normalize token attribution rules: reserved capacity consumption attributed first, then burst pool, then pay-as-you-go if configured
Implement SLA credit worker that computes hourly deviations between reserved SLO and observed throughput and applies configured credit policy (grace window, minimum outage threshold)
Expose reconciliation endpoint and dry-run mode to validate against historical data before enabling billing path
Backfill: run reconciliation over last 90 days for pilot tenants and produce audit report for Finance
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): proto + ingestion, local e2e tests, unit tests for dedupe logic
Phase 2 (staging): wire runtime/gateway emitters, run ingestion in dry-run, compare with existing billing pipeline for 7 days
Phase 3 (canary): route 10 pilot tenants to canonical stream and enable SLA credit worker in dry-run, validate with Customer Success
Phase 4 (gradual): enable canonical billing path for Dedicated pools in 4 waves over 2 weeks, monitor reconciliation dashboards
Phase 5 (full): flip billing-v2 for all Dedicated customers and retire legacy aggregation job after 30 days of stable metrics
testing_plan: Unit tests for dedupe_id collisions and idempotency guarantees
Integration tests that simulate multi-path requests and verify single canonical event emitted
Property tests for token rounding and attribution rules (reserved vs burst vs payg)
Chaos test: drop a subset of gateway events to ensure backfill/ingestion tolerates partial loss without double count
Regression test: run reconciliation on historical incident (INC-2026-004) and confirm SLA credits match expected audit
Load test ingestion pipeline at 10x expected peak to validate throughput and latency constraints
